A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and complete, including v4 Appendices A–C and v5 Appendices A–D. Despite the changed title and substantial revision, the shared adversarial training framework, Sinkhorn procedures and retained proofs clearly identify the same research work.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original transport-error, marginal-violation, convergence-time and generator-ablation experiments. Appendix C provides additional observations of generated training samples.

after.justification: Section 4 and Appendix D report original transport-prediction, barycenter, geodesic, particle-flow, resolution-generalization and variable-regularization experiments.

M1.justification: The primary predictor changes from a fixed-size three-layer MLP to a Fourier Neural Operator with learned Fourier-domain transformations. Squared L2 loss with zero-sum targets replaces the Hilbert loss, and the generator architecture and resolution sampling change. Appendix D.4 adds an epsilon-conditioned input variant; an MLP option remains in Appendix D.2.

E1.justification: The original four image datasets are retained, while v5 adds Quick, Draw! cars, Facial Expressions and cross-dataset transport pairs. Evaluation expands from transport distances and initialization to MNIST and shape barycenters, Wasserstein geodesics and particle flows between distributions over face images.

E2.justification: GeONet becomes an evaluated comparator in v5 Figure 7, whereas v4 only discusses it as related work. Ones and the Gaussian initialization remain the transport-error comparators. Amos et al. is not directly evaluated in either version, and Gaussian timing curves are absent from both versions.

E3.justification: Training changes from 20 million fixed-resolution samples to 200 million samples with randomly selected resolutions between 28×28 and 64×64; target-generation Sinkhorn updates change from 10 to 5. LFW and bear evaluation changes from 28×28 to 64×64. New geometry experiments and resolution/epsilon sweeps introduce additional evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Appendices D.3–D.4 add systematic resolution generalization, extrapolation and joint epsilon/resolution sensitivity analyses. The generator-evolution study is revised. Conversely, v4 Figure 7's controlled comparison of training with generated samples versus random noise is no longer reported.

E5.justification: v4 explicitly reports five independent training runs and 95% confidence intervals for Figures 1, 6, 7 and 8. v5 retains averaging over 500 examples and iteration-count standard deviations, but omits repeated-run and confidence-interval documentation. This substantially reduces reported coverage of training variability; the actual number of v5 training runs is unspecified.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces the MNIST/CIFAR iteration counts of 6±5/8±17 with 3±5/3±6 under the revised model and training settings. v5 adds cross-dataset, geometry and sensitivity results, plus timing ratios ranging from 0.61 on MNIST to 3.46 on CIFAR, while omitting v4's MCV-threshold table. These are not controlled performance gains over v4. Some v5 baseline-curve rankings conflict with Table 1.

T1.justification: v5 adds discretization definitions and a uniform dual-potential convergence argument, extends the bootstrapping bound to mean-zero L2 loss, and introduces barycenter counterexamples and quasi-geodesic reasoning. The retained generator theorem receives an explicit composition bound and proof. The new continuous formulation also introduces a sign inconsistency: Equation 1 subtracts KL divergence, conflicting with its claimed dual and discrete formulation.

C1.justification: v4 emphasizes universal Sinkhorn initialization and standalone distance approximation for fixed dimensions and costs. v5 claims a solver generalizing across both datasets and input resolutions, with accurate transport plans and Wasserstein geometry demonstrated through barycenters and geodesics. This substantially broadens the central contribution.

C2.justification: v4 presents the Hilbert loss's shift invariance as beneficial; v5 Remark B.5 suggests it is an unhelpful learning bias. v5 interprets barycenter results as evidence beyond distance accuracy and adds concrete extrapolation and hardware-dependent runtime qualifications, including slower MNIST inference than Ones. The generator-theorem applicability caveats remain in Appendix C.

D1.justification: v5 documents the FNO and spectral-network architecture, barycenter pseudocode, normalization order and a detailed hyperparameter table. Reported training resources change from about 40 minutes on a V100 to 35 hours on an H100. Code disclosure changes from learn_sink to UNOT and explicitly includes trained model weights.

R1.justification: v5 substantially repositions the work around neural operators and resolution generalization, adding literature on FNOs, Sinkhorn divergences, barycenters and flow matching. Much of v4's VAE, diffusion and normalizing-flow survey disappears. GeONet is the same cited work despite its updated year, but becomes a direct scientific comparison.

P1.justification: The title becomes Universal Neural Optimal Transport, and the abstract, introduction and contribution narrative are extensively rewritten. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 5, discrete OT background largely moves into Appendix A, and the training explanation and appendix organization are substantially restructured.

P2.justification: Existing convergence displays are redesigned and partly moved into Appendix D.6. v5 adds geometry illustrations, an FNO diagram, resolution plots, epsilon heatmaps, and timing and hyperparameter tables, while removing the MCV violin and generator-ablation displays. The Ones/Gauss legends in Figures 3 and 13 produce an ordering inconsistent with Figure 1 and Table 1.

improvement.justification: v5 better supports universality through cross-dataset and resolution tests, and evaluates predicted transport structure through barycenters, geodesics and particle flows, addressing v4's narrow validation scope. Implementation disclosure and concrete applicability limits also improve. These gains are materially offset by removal of the generator ablation and five-run confidence reporting, plus new OT-formulation and baseline-label inconsistencies, leaving a limited net quality improvement.
